figures.caption: TABLE VI: RQ3 failure taxonomy across projects. Percentages are computed over all failure labels in each project.

Fig. 1: Overview of REBUG. The workflow begins with the preparation stage, which reconstructs the required context and produces a reproduction plan. It then enters the execution stage, which performs an iterative execution loop in a real browser with continuous state tracking and trace logging, followed by automatic outcome evaluation.

TABLE III: RQ1 effectiveness and cost of REBUG with different LLM models across four web applications, averaged over multiple independent runs per report. RSR% measures endto-end reproduction success. TCR% denotes the proportion of planned steps completed per run, and AESR% denotes the proportion of actions executed successfully. #Actions, Time (minutes), and #LLM Calls denote per-run means.

TABLE II: RQ1 method comparison using reproduction success rate (RSR). ∆RSR denotes the absolute decrease in RSR (%) relative to the full REBUG configuration with GPT 5 mini on the same dataset. Negative values indicate lower performance compared to REBUG (Full). We include two external baselines: (i) Direct script generation, a one-shot baseline that asks an LLM to synthesize a runnable Playwright or Selenium script from the report, and (ii) Browser-use, a browser agent baseline that drives a real browser without our preparation stage, enhanced tool suite, and execution safeguards.
